title: Changes of State
seo_title: Year 4 Science: Changes of State Worksheets (Melting, Freezing, Boiling, °C)
standard_text: Observe that some materials change state when they are heated or cooled, and measure or research the temperature at which this happens in degrees Celsius (°C).
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on changes of state: melting, freezing, evaporating, boiling and condensing, melting points in °C, thermometers and a heating-ice investigation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Heat or cool to change state.
key_sub: Water melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C; every material has its own melting point.
body_html:
How to think about it

Heating and cooling change the state of a material.

  • Heating: solid → liquid (melting), liquid → gas (evaporating or boiling). Cooling: gas → liquid (condensing), liquid → solid (freezing).
  • Water freezes and melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C. Each material has its own melting point.
  • While ice melts, its temperature stays at 0 °C until all of it has melted.
Example

A puddle dries up. Change?

Liquid → gas

Answer: evaporating

Example

Butter melts at 32 °C. Room at 20 °C?

20 is below 32

Answer: it stays solid

Common mistakes

  • Thinking water boils at 50 °C.
  • Thinking the white cloud over a kettle is steam.
  • Thinking temperature always rises while heating.

faq.q: What are the changes of state?
faq.a: Melting (solid to liquid), freezing (liquid to solid), evaporating or boiling (liquid to gas) and condensing (gas to liquid).

faq.q: At what temperatures does water change state?
faq.a: Pure water freezes and melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C.

faq.q: Why does ice stay at 0 °C while it melts?
faq.a: The heat going in is used to change the ice into water, so the temperature does not rise until all the ice has melted.

items.q: What is the difference between evaporating and boiling?
c: Evaporating happens at the surface at any temperature; boiling happens all through the liquid at the boiling point.
